title: Efondo mango: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Efondo mango: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Efondo mango is a Carabao mango variety from Marciano Efondo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Efondo mango is a Carabao mango variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2005 as NSIC 2005 Mn 07. Marciano Efondo bred it. Its record notes a yield of 833.33 kg.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Efondo mango is grown

blocks.text: The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [mango variety finder](/crop-varieties/mango), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Efondo was about 80 years old and about 15 to 20 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 833.33 kg. It bears every year, with fruit in January February. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit mango fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Mango cecid fly (kurikong)](/pests/mango-cecid-fly), [Mango leafhopper](/pests/mango-leafhopper), [Mango pulp weevil](/pests/mango-pulp-weevil), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Efondo weighs about 341.85 grams, and its shape is ellipsoid. The flesh is yellow orange and firm. Its sweetness measured 18.4 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 80.2 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as January February, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Efondo mango

The Carabao mango is the one the market wants, and the registered strains are its best trees, picked for size, sweetness and steady bearing. Buy grafted seedlings from a BPI accredited nursery so you get the strain you paid for. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Efondo?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
